title: Compositor frame loop: assemble server+layout+vulkan+KMS into internal/compositor
description:
ARCH REVIEW #6 (highest priority). The compositor core junction does not exist: no package ties Wayland surface commits -> layout tick -> Vulkan render -> KMS atomic flip into one loop. cmd/nested-demo is the only glue and renders synthetic quads, not surfaces.

Scope:
- internal/compositor: owns the main event loop (epoll/poll driven: wayland socket + drm fd + timer for tick)
- Surface render path: wl_shm buffer pixels -> vulkan target (or CPU blitter fallback), replacing FrameGrabber's synthetic gradient with real GPU readback or CPU surface copy
- Frame lifecycle: commit -> dirty mark -> tick -> BeginFrame/Draw/EndFrame -> PageFlipAtomic -> flip event -> next tick; define where WaitFrame vs PageFlipNonblock lives
- DOD enforcement at the junction: single-frame benchmark (go test -bench with -benchmem) proving 0 allocs/op across the assembled loop, not per-subsystem
- perf stat L1/LLC profiling of the loop per skills/data-oriented-design.md
- Fake-output test harness: interface for outputs so tests run headless (no DRM master needed) and CI verifies the assembled loop

Acceptance:
- Live display shows real nested-client surfaces (like nested-demo but on KMS)
- 0 allocs/op on the assembled frame benchmark
- Frame loop skippable/none blocking: slow clients cannot stall the scanout thread
- Interface: SurfaceProvider feeding the renderer without FrameGrabber's BGRA-CPU lie

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: Milestone reached live: cmd/bloxwm runs 2 nested foot terminals tiled by the DOD layout engine with full input (pointer motion/buttons + keyboard keys+modifiers flowing sway->backend->ringbuf->router->client). Frame-loop shape proven in the shm-blit demo; o2x replaces the blit with Vulkan+DMA-BUF on this same ownership model (one renderer owner, coalesced redraw requests). Also: parent-socket run loop must retry EINTR/EAGAIN — silent exits kill input.

title: bloxwm-session: supervisor process (parent of compositor + clients, restart + respawn)
description:
A long-lived supervisor that owns the session environment and is the parent of BOTH the compositor and the clients it spawns, so restarting the compositor does not kill the kids.

Design (option A, agreed):
- cmd/bloxwm-session: sets up env (WAYLAND_DISPLAY, XDG_*), listens on a control socket (/run/user/1000/bloxwm-session.sock), spawns the compositor as its child, auto-restarts it on exit (rate-limited), and spawns clients on request so they are ITS children (survive compositor death).
- Control protocol (line-based over the unix socket): SPAWN <cmd...>, STOP, RESTART, STATUS. bloxwm's spawn action talks to it when BLOXWM_SESSION_SOCKET is set; otherwise execs directly (current behaviour).
- Respawn-lite: the supervisor records every SPAWN (argv, cwd, env subset). When the compositor restarts, it relaunches the recorded clients so the on-screen session comes back automatically. This is respawn, NOT resume — on-screen Wayland apps still die with their connection (no protocol-state handoff; that is option B, explicitly out of scope).

Tests (no compositor needed): supervisor starts a long-lived dummy child and a dummy compositor; killing the compositor triggers restart while the child survives; SPAWN over the socket creates a child parented to the supervisor; recorded children are relaunched after a compositor restart; STOP tears everything down. Rate-limit a crash-looping compositor.

Out of scope: Wayland connection survival / state replay (option B).
close_reason: Supervisor daemon + control protocol + compositor spawn routing, tests + live-verified. 7687896

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: Landed 7687896. Supervisor + control socket + daemon + compositor spawn routing. Design decisions: (1) children are Setsid'd so signalling the supervisor's group never reaches them, but are reaped by the supervisor; (2) compositor and clients get SEPARATE envs — a nested compositor must keep its parent's WAYLAND_DISPLAY while spawned clients get ours; (3) respawn-lite relaunches only DEAD children (pid-tracked per record) and updates the record in place, so survivors are never duplicated and the record set does not grow across restarts (adversarial review caught the append-per-respawn bug). Tests: restart-keeps-child-alive, respawn-dead-child, SPAWN-over-socket, STOP-teardown, crash-loop guard, newline rejection, no-record-growth. Live: nested bloxwm under supervisor, spawned child survived two compositor restarts, dead child relaunched, STOP cleaned up.

title: Compose wl_subsurfaces (parsed but never rendered)
description:
The server parses wl_subcompositor/wl_subsurface (get_subsurface, set_position, place_above/below, set_sync/desync) but the compositor never renders subsurfaces: the scene is windows + popups only, and the subsurface handlers are no-ops. Impact: foot uses subsurfaces for client-side decorations; video players (mpv), GTK apps and anything doing sub-surface video/overlays render nothing or misplace content.

Fix: model a subsurface tree per parent surface (position, stacking, sync/desync), place it relative to the parent's body rect in the scene (below popups, above the parent), and composite it with the parent's transform. Sync subsurfaces must be committed atomically with the parent (cache pending state until the parent commits). Tests: a parent + one subsurface at a non-zero offset renders at the right place; sync mode defers until parent commit; desync renders immediately; stacking order honoured.

Also verify the parse side: WlSubsurfaceHandler callbacks exist and are registered (ObjSubsurface dispatch row present).
close_reason: Server subsurface model (position/sync/desync/stacking) + commit propagation + actor placement/rendering. Tests: real-wire lifecycle + actor placement/order/cleanup. Live-verified rendering. 97c4230

title: o2x phase 4: KMS scanout presents the Vulkan target (drop the BridgeTo readback)
description:
Replace the phase-3 bridge (GPU target -> CPU readback -> nested shm) with direct scanout: Vulkan renders into a KMS dumb buffer imported as the render target (zero copy, zero CPU), then drmModeAddFB2 + atomic modeset once + PageFlipAtomic per frame.

Design (zero-copy render-to-scanout):
- KMS: CreateDumbBuffer(w,h) + PrimeExport + AddFB2 + Destroy/RemoveFB methods on Card (dumb alloc and AddFB2 need no DRM master, so unit-testable under sway).
- Vulkan: render-target-from-DMA-BUF path (import the scanout fd with COLOR_ATTACHMENT usage + framebuffer; linear-tiling SRGB render target). Falls back to the existing optimal target + bridge if linear render is unsupported.
- cmd/bloxwm: BLOXWM_KMS=1 selects the KMS backend; output size comes from the connector preferred mode; SetModeAtomic once, PageFlipAtomic per presented frame; input still via nested/evdev as today.
- Tests: dumb/FB helpers without master; target-from-fd import; scanout loop with a fake flip; live modeset+flip verified on a VT (master required - user-assisted, documented).

Non-goals: multi-output, cursor plane, gamma, VkImageDrmFormatModifier probing (linear dumb is the contract).

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: Wiring landed (bea8692): BLOXWM_KMS=1 selects bare-metal (KMS display, scanout executor, evdev input); output sized from preferred mode; graceful VT hint when master busy. Proven without master (alloc/export/import/render/output-adapter). Remaining: live modeset+flip on a VT. To verify: switch to VT (Ctrl+Alt+F3), log in, run 'BLOXWM_KMS=1 BLOXWM_GPU=1 /path/to/bin/bloxwm' — expect KMS modeset line + direct scanout. Input via evdev (keyboard required in video/input groups or root).

title: compositor core: single-owner scene state (actor model) — retire the shared-mu callback graph
description:
ARCH FIX (user call-out: 'deadlocks are smelly'). Second lock-order incident in cmd/bloxwm: onClientDestroy held mu and invoked router.SetFocus, whose onFocusChange callback takes mu — non-reentrant deadlock, silent screen freeze (3ea5edc fixed the instance, not the class). The class: state guarded by one mu, mutated from N goroutine contexts (server callbacks, input pump, renderer), plus callbacks that re-acquire mu — every new call edge risks a freeze with zero diagnostics (no panic, no trace).

TARGET ARCHITECTURE (the o2x frame loop generalized):
- ONE goroutine owns all scene state: windows map, engine, activeWin, focus. No shared mutex.
- Everything else talks to it via messages: server callbacks, input pump, and renderer submit events (windowAdded, windowRemoved, surfaceCommitted, focusMoved, redrawTick) into an event queue the owner drains
- The renderer stays a separate goroutine but receives immutable scene snapshots (already the DrawList contract) — it never blocks on state
- Backpressure: coalescing redraw channel stays; state events are cheap, no queue growth beyond window count
- Wire-level handlers (server.Client) stay as-is; the shell (cmd/bloxwm) becomes: callbacks = channel sends only, zero shared state

MIGRATION PATH:
1. internal/compositor: SceneStore type owning windows+focus+activeWin, event-queue drained by the frame loop goroutine (the loop currently only renders; it becomes the compositor actor)
2. cmd/bloxwm callbacks become sends; delete mu entirely from the shell
3. Deadlock class disappears BY CONSTRUCTION — no shared lockable state
4. DOD alignment: state on one goroutine, flat records flowing one direction (input -> state -> render), no cross-goroutine mutation — matches the input ring-buffer pattern already used

ACCEPTANCE:
- grep: no mu in cmd/bloxwm beyond the backend's own
- -race clean with 2 clients + teardown storms
- The lock-order contract comment at the focus-fall site becomes obsolete (delete it)
close_reason: Actor model landed: shell callbacks = channel sends, one owner goroutine owns scene state and renders (zero mutexes in cmd/bloxwm), router focus commands queued via focusReq applied on its own loop, hit-testing via atomic.Pointer scene snapshot. The deadlock class is gone by construction. Live-verified with 2 nested feet; -race green.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: Design formulation (user): 'callbacks sound like a channel to me' — exactly. The existing srv.SetOn*/nested.Callbacks registrations stay as the seams; each callback body becomes a single non-blocking channel send of a plain-data event into the owner goroutine's queue. The owner drains events, mutates scene state, snapshots to the renderer. Concretely: events <- Event{Kind: evCommitted, ClientID, SurfaceID}. No shared state, no lock-order contracts to remember — the deadlock class is gone by construction.

title: CI + quality gates: lint, vet, race, and 0-alloc benchmark assertions
description:
ARCH REVIEW #7. No CI definition, no lint beyond go vet, and the 0-allocs DOD mandate is enforced only by convention (benchmarks exist but nothing fails when they regress).

Scope:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (or repo CI of choice): go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... (short mode so live-daemon/KMS tests skip fast), gofmt -l check
- golangci-lint config: govet, staticcheck, errcheck, unused, gofmt; exclude generated protocol files
- DOD gate: benchmark harness step that runs the zero-alloc hot-path benchmarks (layout engine, wire decoder, input pump, pipewire framing, vulkan frame) and FAILS if allocs/op > 0 — use testing.Bench with a threshold script or -run nothing + bench comparison (go benchstat against committed baseline)
- perf stat L1/LLC miss profiling as a nightly/manual job, not a merge gate (hardware-dependent)
- Race build: go test -race ./... on the assembled loop once bloxwm-o2x exists

Acceptance: CI green on main; intentionally adding an alloc to a hot path fails CI

title: dbus Reader: handle partial reads + oversized replies (recvReply misparses split frames)
description:
ARCH REVIEW #5a. internal/portal/dbus/conn.go recvReply() assumes one Read returns one complete message. Unlike the pipewire recvMsg accumulator (which handles partial/multiple packets), dbus recvReply:
- A reply split across reads >4096 byte read chunk misparses (DecodeHeader fails on partial buffer, loop re-reads and appends but the greedy parse logic only re-checks the whole accumulated buffer once per read — on success it returns, but a message larger than one read chunk arrives across chunks and the current code CAN eventually parse it; however it also silently drops unrelated interleaved signals/events without buffering discipline)
- No length-based framing: it cannot know how many bytes the next message needs except by decode success
- Error path: interleaved signals between call and reply are discarded unparsed (fine for the minimal client) but a partially-received signal can be concatenated with the reply — cross-message corruption

Scope:
- Port the pipewire rolling-accumulator pattern: keep pending []byte, decode header, check total span (fieldsEnd aligned + bodyLen), consume exact bytes, keep remainder
- Handle TypeError bodies (error name + message) without misparsing
- Test: stub bus that replies in two 40-byte chunks (byte-splits the message mid-header and mid-body); assert reply parsed correctly
- Shared primitives: extract align/pad helpers into internal/alignio if bloxwm-o2x touches this layer first; otherwise keep local
close_reason: recvReply now uses a rolling accumulator with MessageTotalSpan framing: interleaved complete messages are skipped exactly, replies split across reads are assembled correctly. Stub test drives split frames mid-header plus interleaved signal. Full suite green.

title: Remove hardcoded fabric: output geometry, client identity props, fd-slot caps
description:
ARCH REVIEW #3. Hardcoded values scattered across packages will break silently when any one is changed.

Scope:
1. Virtual output geometry (960x640) appears literally in internal/server/capture.go outputResolution() and client.go HandleWlRegistryBind wl_output mode. One source of truth: Output struct in server (width/height/refresh) set once at startup, wl_output events and capture session buffer_size both read from it. Capture buffer validation must reference the same source.
2. UpdateClientProperties (internal/pipewire/conn.go) hardcodes 'phil', 'phil-desktop', 'en_GB.UTF-8' and a hand-counted dict Int(6). Replace with os/user.Current() + golang.org/x/sys/unix.Uname for host/kernel, locale from env; derive n_items from the actual slice length (mismatched count = silent protocol corruption).
3. Fixed [4]int fd slots (internal/wire/message.go, internal/pipewire/framing.go) silently truncate staged fds. Size dynamically or document+assert the cap with a test.

Acceptance:
- grep finds no literal 'phil' in non-test code
- wl_output mode and capture buffer_size come from one struct
- Test: UpdateClientProperties dict n_items equals entries encoded
close_reason: Output geometry single-sourced (Server.Output feeds wl_output + capture), client identity derived from process/env with dict count derived from data, fd staging verified safe (wire errors on overflow, pipewire appends/grows). Tests added for geometry source-of-truth and dict count. Verified live: handshake+registry still green with derived identity.

title: pipewire: deterministic stub-daemon tests for handshake/registry (live tests skip in CI)
description:
ARCH REVIEW #2. The repo's most valuable assets are empirical protocol facts (sequential proxy ids, zero default perms until props update, sync batching, stream framing) but they are only verified by tests that silently SKIP without a live pipewire daemon — CI would be green while the code rots.

Scope:
- internal/pipewire/stub_test.go: SOCK_STREAM stub daemon implementing the pw native protocol server side for exactly the client path: header parse (opcode top-byte/size low-24/seq/fds), Hello -> Struct{Int(4)} demarshal -> core_info reply, client.update_properties -> client_info reply, get_registry -> N synthetic global events + core.done, registry.bind -> proxy accept
- Assert: framing byte-exactness (opcode in word2 top byte), seq increment, sequential id rule (reject id>mapsize with ENOSPC-shaped error like the real daemon), zero-globals-before-props-update behavior replicated from the live daemon findings
- Add testdata fixture: committed pw-cli strace hex capture (from /tmp/opencode/pwcli_hex.txt — re-capture before committing since /tmp is volatile) to pin framing against a known-good client
- Same pattern for portal/dbus: deterministic stub already exists (good — copy the pattern)

Acceptance:
- go test ./internal/pipewire passes with no daemon running (no skips)
- The live-daemon tests remain as extra verification (skip-able) but are no longer the only coverage
close_reason: Stub daemon implements the client connect path server-side (Hello demarshal, core_info, client props, get_registry with sequential-id enforcement, sync/done, zero-globals-before-props rule). Tests run with no daemon (no skips); real pw-cli capture committed as testdata fixture. Live tests still pass.

title: server/core: split Client god object into DOD-oriented stores
description:
ARCH REVIEW #1. internal/server/client.go is 1172 lines; Client owns objects, pools, buffers, surfaces, xdgSurfaces, xdgToplevels, capture state, input focus, data-device — all as heap pointer-graph slices under one coarse c.mu.

Scope:
- Introduce generational SlotMap object tables (per AGENTS.md DOD: WindowID-style uint32 gen+index) for surfaces, buffers, pools; SoA arrays for hot fields (geometry rects, state flags) and cold fields (titles) split
- Replace findObject/findBuffer/findPool linear scans with direct-index lookups
- Locking: split coarse c.mu — object table hot-path lock vs slow-path protocol state; audit the capture.go unlock-relock grab path (HandleExtImageCopyCaptureFrameV1Capture) for a defined ownership model instead of hand-verified invariants
- dispatch() switch: keep flat but driven by a table (objType -> dispatcher) generated or initialized once, not extended per-protocol by hand
- Blast radius constraint: protocol handlers keep working unchanged; this is a storage/restructuring change under the same handlers

Acceptance:
- All existing server tests pass unchanged
- New race tests: concurrent surface commits + capture grab with -race
- Escape analysis audit: no per-message heap escapes in dispatch (go build -gcflags=-m) for the hot decode path
close_reason: Phases 1-3 complete: generational object table + table-driven dispatch (missing-dispatcher bug class now caught by tests), typed O(1) stores migrated across all handlers (surfaces/buffers/pools/xdg), race test pinning the under-c.mu table invariant, capture-grab ownership contract documented for o2x (pool pinning required before render-thread grabs). Escape analysis shows only init-time allocs; hot-path 0-alloc verification happens in o2x's assembled-loop benchmark. All server tests green incl. -race.

title: Spike: FFI approach to renderer — audit/cost against cgo-embedded C Vulkan core
description:
The renderer is not really Go: internal/render/vulkan/renderer.go and device.go embed the hot core as C via cgo (VkRenderer, begin_frame, draw_texture_quad, descriptor ring, import_dmabuf_buffer). Go is a shim over C functions. The o2x session's debugging pain (C-side state read from Go, silent inPass=0, descriptor aliasing, fence ownership) all traced to that boundary.

Spike goal: prototype ONE slice of the renderer in pure Go over the Vulkan C ABI (no cgo wrapper per call) and answer, with numbers and a working diff:

1. Binding approach: hand-written syscall/dlopen against libvulkan.so via unsafe + vkGetInstanceProcAddr, vs cgo with real Vulkan headers (types checked, still C), vs a Go binding generator from vk.xml (vk-go style). Recommend one.
2. Cost: ns/op and allocs/op for the frame-loop hot path (BeginFrame/draw/EndFrame) Go-vs-current-cgo; must hold the 0-allocs/op DOD bar.
3. Fencing/ownership: can the begin_frame-waits-then-resets invariant and the readback-fence bug class be expressed in Go so it is testable at the language level rather than discovered by pixel diff?
4. Blast radius: which of internal/render/vulkan survives (shaders/SPR-V gen, device selection, ImportDmaBuf) vs gets rewritten.

Non-goals: no rewrite in the spike; do not touch the working nested path; no KMS scope (o2x phase 4 continues on the current renderer).

Deliverable: a spike report bead + a small prototype branch/cmd showing the approach on one function (e.g. vkQueueSubmit or draw_color_quad), with the benchmark and a go/no-go recommendation. Definition of done: numbers from this machine (AMD RENOIR, RADV), a written recommendation, and either a filed follow-up bead for the migration plan or a documented 'stay cgo' rationale.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: User steering: the goal is not just language purity - it is RUNTIME INDEPENDENCE. A software renderer mode with no libvulkan dependency at all (binary runs on systems without Vulkan userspace). Reframing the spike: evaluate whether a pure-Go FFI binding can make the compositor's fallback CPU path (shm blitter) the primary non-Vulkan path, and whether the Vulkan dependency can become load-time optional rather than build-time required. This changes Q2/Q3: the deliverable should also measure a HEADLESS/software rasteriser path (Go blitter is already 0-alloc in internal/compositor CPUExecutor) and assess dlopen-vs-build-link so bloxwm binary still runs when libvulkan.so is absent.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: Clarification on how the current build works, for scoping: today the Vulkan core is compiled INTO the binary via cgo (it does not dlopen libvulkan at runtime for its own API - it links libvulkan.so through the loader, and the driver is dlopen'd by the loader). So bloxwm already fails to start without the Vulkan loader present. A software/dependency-free mode means: (a) build-time option to exclude the Vulkan renderer entirely (BuildTag), leaving CPUExecutor + a shm/KMS target, or (b) runtime dlopen of the Vulkan loader with graceful fallback. Spike should decide which of these two actually meets the 'runs without vulkan libs' requirement, and measure the CPUExecutor blit path end to end (ns/op, allocs/op, and wall clock per frame at 1280x720) so the fallback is a real choice, not a toy.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: DECISION (user): option (a) build-tag exclusion is rejected - single binary or nothing. The spike is scoped to (b) RUNTIME DLOPEN: the compositor must dlopen the Vulkan loader (or its driver backend) at runtime, work when present, and fall back to the pure-Go CPU renderer when absent, in ONE binary. Implications: cgo's build-time linking cannot produce that binary, so option (b) is not compatible with the current cgo renderer - it REQUIRES the FFI work. The spike therefore becomes the critical path for this goal, not an optional language exercise. Acceptance: build one binary, run it on this machine with libvulkan present (GPU mode) and with the loader hidden (LD_LIBRARY_PATH/LD_PRELOAD trick or a chroot-ish run), and confirm automatic fallback to the CPU renderer with no crash and no build flag.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text:
SPIKE RESULTS (step 1: loader model + FFI cost, measured on this machine, go1.25.4 linux/amd64):

FINDING 1 - the runtime-dlopen goal is achievable with ONE tiny cgo file: a probe with only dlopen/dlsym C shims links ZERO vulkan (ldd | grep -c vulkan = 0) while the current binary links libvulkan.so.1 at build time (=1). That is the shape that satisfies 'runs without vulkan libs': the binary is only libc-dependent; libvulkan is resolved via dlopen(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_GLOBAL) + vkGetInstanceProcAddr. dlopen(nil) when absent -> clean fallback, no crash (probe_missing).

FINDING 2 - per-call FFI hop cost: C call through cgo = 33.9 ns/op vs 2.4 ns/op for an equivalent Go call (~14x). Current design does ONE cgo call per quad => 138 ns/op for 4 quads; batching the whole frame into one cgo call => 32 ns/op. At 60fps and <64 quads/frame the per-call overhead is noise (<1% of a 16ms frame), so cost is NOT the blocker - correctness/state ownership was.

FINDING 3 (honest limitation, needs your call): a FULLY cgo-free dlopen (CGO_ENABLED=0) is not practically available - glibc dlopen is not a syscall, and hand-rolling an ELF loader to resolve dlopen is fragile to the point of being irresponsible. So the plan is: keep one small cgo file that ONLY does dlopen/dlsym (no Vulkan headers, no -lvulkan at link time), and move the entire renderer core into pure Go calling resolved function pointers. Binary still links libc (it already does), never links vulkan.

NEXT: step 2 = prototype the pure-Go dispatch table over the resolved vkGetInstanceProcAddr for BeginFrame/draw/EndFrame with real buffers, then benchmark Go-vs-cgo frame path end to end.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: STEP 2 COMPLETE — pure-Go frame slice proven on live hardware (RADV RENOIR). spikevk/ now drives instance -> logical device -> offscreen target -> clear -> copy -> mapped readback with correct pixels, all through runtime-resolved addresses. One binary, zero libvulkan at link (ldd), absent loader fails cleanly. Numbers: 1280x720 steady-state 15.8ms/frame (GPU submit/wait latency dominates, not FFI); 8 allocs/op from cgo per-call overhead (batching to one call/frame recovers ~0). ABI firewall (46 sizes + 26 offsets) pins struct transcription. Full suite green. GO/NO-GO: technically GO — the blocker was never the hop (34ns) but state ownership, and the spike shows Go can own the whole frame path testably. Remaining before migration: textured-quad crate (shaders/pipelines) + the one-call-per-frame batch design; file those as the follow-up, or close this as 'GO with plan'.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: CRATE COMPLETE (bloxwm-bk0 closed): textured quads render correctly in pure Go — render pass, framebuffer, sampler, Go descriptor ring, pipeline from production SPIR-V, staging upload, draws, readback. TestQuadTwoTexturesVisible + TestQuadUploadRoundtrip green and validation-clean; BenchmarkTexturedFrame 16.8ms / 10 allocs per 1280x720 frame (allocs are envelope closures; batch design recovers). Remaining open item from the bead: the one-call-per-frame batch design evaluation — file separately if wanted, since per-call cost is already <1% and batching is purely an allocs optimisation now.

comments.author: Phil Richards
comments.text: BATCH DONE (bloxwm-ewo closed): BenchmarkTexturedFrame 10 allocs -> 0 B / 0 allocs per 1280x720 frame, pixels exact (TestQuad* green). Single UpdateDescriptorSets(N), reused C scratch for rpBegin/submit, all C-crossing structs as renderer fields. Per-draw bind/push/draw stay Go calls by design; draw-batching-into-C rejected as agreed. Full repo suite (18 pkgs) green.

title: Shared io primitives: single SCM_RIGHTS staging + alignment helpers across wire/dbus/pipewire
description:
ARCH REVIEW #5b. Three protocol layers (internal/wire, internal/portal/dbus, internal/pipewire) duplicate: alignment-padding loops (3 copies, subtly different rules per protocol), SCM_RIGHTS fd staging/parsing (2+ copies), rolling-read accumulation (2 copies, one with the partial-read bug tracked in bloxwm-ssd).

Scope:
- internal/alignio (or internal/ioutils): PadTo(buf, n), AlignedLen, ReadAligned32/64, small header framing helper — protocol-agnostic
- Each codec keeps its own domain semantics (Wayland 4-align vs D-Bus message-relative vs POD 8-align) but reuses the pad/align math
- FD staging: one primitive with a documented cap and error behavior, used by wire and pipewire writers
- Rolling accumulator: one implementation with pluggable header-length/total-span decoders (function params) used by dbus and pipewire conns

Constraints (per AGENTS.md general-guidelines: no premature abstraction, blast radius local):
- Only extract what is already duplicated 2+ times (pad, fd stage, accumulator). Do NOT force a common Reader/Writer interface over the three codecs — their domain types differ legitimately
- Land AFTER bloxwm-o2x touches these layers, or atomically with it, to avoid a moving target

title: portal/dbus: TestRecvReplySplitAndInterleaved is flaky (handshake read framing in the test stub)
description: The stub goroutine in internal/portal/dbus/split_test.go reads one c.Read per protocol message and assumes each client send is a separate read. Under -race and load the Hello and the tracked call can coalesce (or arrive before the stub reads), so a later Read returns 0/err and the stub closes the connection early; the client then fails with 'write: broken pipe' on c.send. Reproduced ~6/10 with -count=10 (pre-existing: ~12/10 counting the data race also fixed alongside). Fix: frame reads in the stub (read full D-Bus messages by length) or drive it off a message count rather than blind Read calls. Unrelated to the live binary (internal/portal is unwired).
close_reason: Stub now frames reads by D-Bus message length after reading the AUTH/BEGIN control lines precisely; 20 -race runs clean. e3f6d40

title: Spike 1h7 follow-up: batch descriptor updates + reuse C scratch (NOT draw batching)
description:
Pure-Go textured frame measures 10 allocs / 344 B per 1280x720 op. At least 4 are envelope() closures (one per envelope: render-pass-begin, 2x descriptor writes, submit); the rest is cgo per-call overhead. Wall time (16.8ms) is GPU-dominated, so this is about the 0-alloc bar, not speed.

Do:
1. Descriptor-update batching: build all N VkWriteDescriptorSet in Go, envelope once, single UpdateDescriptorSets(count=N) instead of N calls.
2. Scratch reuse: replace per-call envelope (malloc + closure alloc) with one C scratch buffer per frame object, written via Go stores. Kills all envelope allocs.

Explicitly rejected: (3) draw batching (one C call looping over draws). It would move draw logic back into C and defeat the spike's Go-ownership goal, for no meaningful wall-time gain.

Definition of done: BenchmarkTexturedFrame reports ~0 allocs/op with no change to rendered pixels (TestQuadTwoTexturesVisible still green), and the envelope-closure pattern is gone from the hot path.
close_reason: Closed
